name: Carnivore diet smell
lead: Carnivore diet smell refers to claims about how an all-animal-product diet affects body odour, breath and sweat. Some adherents say their odour becomes milder, while others report the opposite.[1]

The carnivore diet is a high-protein, low-carbohydrate diet limited to meat, dairy and eggs; Wikipedia says nutrition bodies list it among fad diets and that it has no supporting clinical evidence.[2] That article does not discuss body odour, and no study found here has measured odour on the diet.

paras: The carnivore diet excludes fruit, vegetables, grains, legumes, nuts and seeds, and its strictest form permits only beef, salt and water.[2] Body odour in general is attributed to skin bacteria acting on gland secretions, with diet and gut microbiome among listed influences.[1] A study cited on Wikipedia found that men eating more fruit and vegetables had sweat rated as more pleasant, though this did not test an animal-only diet.[1]
Wikipedia notes that high intake of carnitine or choline can contribute to fishy odour in the secondary form of trimethylaminuria, and that red meat is high in carnitine.[3]

lore.intro: Discussion is largely anecdotal, with some users saying odour improves and others reporting stronger smells.

claims.claim: Eating only meat makes body odour neutral or less noticeable.
claims.believers: Proponents say removing plant foods leaves sweat and stool less pungent.
claims.experts: No published studies of carnivore-diet odour were found; a separate study linked more fruit and vegetables to more pleasant sweat ratings.[1]

claims.claim: Carnivore eating can cause a stronger or fishy smell.
claims.believers: Some adherents report stronger odour or breath changes.
claims.experts: High carnitine and choline intake is described as a trigger in secondary trimethylaminuria.[3]

card.summary: Claims that eating only meat changes how you smell; reports go both ways and no one has measured it.
card.note: Anecdotal; the diet itself is criticised by dietitians' bodies.

quick.overview:
Followers of all-meat diets often say their body odour changes, sometimes for the better and sometimes not.

No study found here has measured odour on such a diet.
quick.mechanism: Skin bacteria break down gland secretions, and diet is one listed influence. Meat is high in carnitine and choline, which gut bacteria can convert to compounds with a fishy smell in susceptible people.
quick.risks: Wikipedia says dietitian bodies list the carnivore diet among fad diets, citing risks such as lacking fibre, raised LDL cholesterol and nutrient gaps.[2]
